title: CRC tests use self-referential oracle (crc32fast hashes both sides)
description:
In yencoding-multi/tests/integration.rs, all CRC tests that call set_expected_crc32() compute the expected value via crc32fast::hash() — the same crate that finish() uses internally. This means the CRC path only proves crc32fast::hash == crc32fast::hash, not that the assembled data has the correct CRC.

Affected tests: three_parts_in_order, three_parts_out_of_order, missing_middle_part, duplicate_part_rejected, sweep_sizes_round_trip (via encode_and_assemble helper), and roundtrip_via_yencoding_encode_part in assembler.rs.

The crc_mismatch_on_finish test uses a hardcoded 0xdeadbeef which is a proper negative test, but no positive CRC test uses an independently-computed expected value.

Fix: replace at least one set_expected_crc32() call with a value computed externally, e.g.:
  Python: binascii.crc32(bytes(range(90))) & 0xFFFFFFFF
  OpenSSL: echo -n ... | openssl dgst ...
Hardcode that value as a hex literal in the test.
